sub_scenario.family: rehearsal load versus protected voice clarity
sub_scenario.one_line: union apprenticeship coordinator: accept a daytime rehearsal in the hall, not the Thursday night setup

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the skills matrix and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The trade calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can make a quick attendance announcement on the shop floor.
That does not take sustained projection.
It is over before my voice warms up.
Someone new shadowed me in the apprenticeship hall this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the assessment weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On 9 January, I ran one safety-demonstration rehearsal after instructors commented on the cue sheet overnight.
How did you perform at the certification assessment?
I was audible through every station and could answer follow-ups.
I draft demonstration cues with the instructors in a shared document.
Could the crew review cues before meeting?
Yes, then rehearsal is for timing rather than reciting every step.
I archived last cycle's notes on the trade calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
You handled an all-day bargaining session last autumn.
I did, but I was not demonstrating over machinery and had the following morning free.
The vocal conditions were not alike.
A vendor call about the skills matrix ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the apprenticeship hall checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the assessment weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the trade calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On 22 March, a late rehearsal beside active compressors ran for nearly three hours before a 08:00 crane-safety assessment.
What did the assessment require?
I could not project the stop signals reliably, so another coordinator covered that station.
I sketched next week's plan for the assessment weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the skills matrix updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I am in voice therapy after a bout of laryngitis; my therapist specifically has me limiting loud evening speech during recovery.
Is a written cue review still workable?
Yes, that is exactly the alternative I am using.
I compared two options for the trade calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the apprenticeship hall handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Is the Thursday night rehearsal beside the compressors a good slot for me before Friday's crane-safety assessment?
